newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes at fresh recent low, heads lower.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes at fresh recent low, heads lower.

text.p: Gold prices slumped on Thursday afternoon after news the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had the necessary majority to sell five million ounces of gold from its reserves.
Gold was fixed at $380.45 after $382.05 this morning. It was the lowest gold fix since September 6, 1995.
The low fix followed a statement from IMF head Michel Camdessus that the organisation had a majority in favour of selling gold to help the world's poorest nations.
Earlier investment fund selling had put pressure on an already soggy market.
"Everybody was saying they wanted to see $380 at the expiry. In fact the number was reached before that," one dealer said.
In the event, the over-the-counter options expiry had no impact on the price.
Now gold was targetting $378.00 support with some dealers forecasting a bounce off $379.00 to $383.00.
Platinum recorded its lowest fixing since January 31, 1994 at $385.25 per ounce beating its previous recent low on September 23 of $386.50, the lowest since April 20, 1994.
The fixing took 35 minutes and after a couple of good sellers came in, selling spread rapidly, dealers said.
Platinum has been under pressure since it fell down through $390.00 earlier this month.
Dealers said consumers were content to live off their stocks while the market was apparently oversupplied and weakening.
Its narrow premium over gold was adding to the pressure given that it was being sustained by spread players buying platinum and selling gold.
"There was always the risk of platinum coming down if the spread plays stopped," one dealer said.
At 1445 GMT platinum was indicated at $384.00/$385.00 down from $387.50/$388.50 at the previous close.
Silver and palladium were relatively unscathed by the falls in gold and platinum although both of them have looked weak and vulnerable recently.
Silver was indicated at $4.86/$4.88 down five cents from the close and palladiuim was at $117.75/$118.75, down $1.25.
